lines: Welcome to Module Three: Evaluation and Tuning.
How do you measure a system with no single right answer?
Picture an insurer's AI assistant that answers questions about claims.
In every demo it felt great, so the team shipped it.
Then someone tweaked the prompt to sound friendlier.
Nobody noticed that wrong coverage answers quietly doubled.
The team had no metrics, just a feeling.
And one end-to-end score would only say something broke, never where.
So they added an AI judge to grade the answers.
It loved long, confident replies, even the wrong ones.
Next, they planned to fine-tune the model on policy documents.
But policies change every quarter, and fine-tuning bakes facts into the weights.
Instead, they tested each piece alone, starting with retrieval, the search step.
The right policy clause was never being fetched at all.
They also checked trajectories, the path the agent took.
Some right answers came after six redundant tool calls and a lucky guess.
They rebuilt the judge to compare answers in pairs, with a clear rubric.
Then they checked it against human experts before trusting its scores.
The real fix was better retrieval, not fine-tuning.
And a golden test set now runs on every change, so no tweak slips through.
Lesson one shows what to measure: components, steps, trajectories, and outcomes.
Plus how to test on real traffic safely, with shadow and canary rollouts.
Agents vary from run to run, so one run proves nothing.
Passing once in k tries shows capability; passing every time shows reliability.
